summary: Reproduced the apparent throughput mismatch and established that request-level whole-lifetime TPOT and the engine's recent-window aggregate token rate have different scopes. Added a benchmark output note that identifies those scopes and points aggregate comparisons to whole-run output throughput; metric formulas and the stable engine log field are unchanged.

tests.what_was_measured: Real gfx950 serving path: bench output throughput 1499.91 tok/s, mean/median TPOT 2.16/2.14 ms, measured concurrency 3.72, and steady engine reporting windows 1918.36-1934.43 tok/s.
Regression failed during collection because format_metric_scope_note did not exist.
Two independent wording boundary checks passed: client/request lifetime versus engine/recent window, and no invalid TPOT-times-concurrency equivalence.
Real gfx950 post-change serving output contained the scope note; bench output throughput was 1480.49 tok/s and steady engine windows were 1821.60-1848.46 tok/s.

remaining_limitations: The reported Qwen2.5-0.5B weights were unavailable, so no model-architecture or semantic claim is made.
The assigned GPU is AMD gfx950, not the report's NVIDIA H800/CUDA system.
The qualified fixture's 128-token context and four-request capacity cannot reproduce the original 2048-input/256-output, concurrency-16 workload.
The evidence establishes metric scope and serving behavior, not performance equivalence across GPU vendors or model sizes.
